subject: English Literature
title: XI. Précis Writing and Essay Composition

segments.text: Précis writing (talkhees nawesi) is a core compositional and comprehension skill tested in Urdu-medium examination contexts, requiring the systematic condensation of a longer passage into a shorter, accurate, and well-organised summary that preserves the original’s essential meaning and logical structure.
Core requirements of effective précis writing.

An effective précis must accurately capture the original passage’s central argument and essential supporting points while eliminating illustrative detail, repetition, and rhetorical elaboration not essential to the core meaning; must maintain proportional balance across the original passage’s various sections, reflecting each section’s relative importance in the original rather than disproportionately compressing or expanding particular parts; must be expressed in the writer’s own words and sentence structures rather than merely extracting and stringing together phrases lifted directly from the original passage, demonstrating genuine comprehension rather than simple mechanical excerption; and must typically conform to a specified word limit (commonly expressed as a specific proportion, such as one-third, of the original passage’s length), requiring disciplined, deliberate selection of genuinely essential content.

These include excessive length (failing to achieve genuine, disciplined condensation); omission of genuinely essential points (sacrificing accuracy and completeness for brevity); disproportionate treatment (over-emphasising minor points while under-representing the original’s actual main argument); mechanical copying of the original’s specific phrasing rather than genuine paraphrase; and loss of logical coherence (producing a précis that reads as a disconnected list of extracted points rather than a coherent, well-organised piece of connected prose in its own right).

Effective précis writing generally proceeds through careful initial reading to identify the passage’s central argument and logical structure, identification of essential versus illustrative/supporting content, drafting in the writer’s own words while maintaining the original’s logical sequence and proportional emphasis, and careful final revision against the specified word limit and against the original passage to verify accuracy and completeness of the core argument.

items.text: Effective précis writing requires accurately capturing a passage’s central argument while eliminating inessential detail, maintaining proportional balance, using original wording rather than mechanical excerption, and observing a specified word limit.

Common errors include excessive length, omission of essential points, disproportionate treatment of minor versus major content, mechanical copying rather than genuine paraphrase, and loss of logical coherence.

Effective practice requires careful initial reading for structure and argument, disciplined selection of essential content, original-wording drafting, and careful final revision against both the word limit and the original passage’s accuracy.

segments.text: Urdu essay writing (mazmoon nawesi) is a core compositional skill requiring the sustained, well-organised development of an argument or exposition on a given topic, drawing on the full range of rhetorical, structural, and stylistic resources of formal Urdu prose.

An effective Urdu essay typically follows a clear structural logic: an engaging, well-framed introduction (aghaz) establishing the topic’s significance and the essay’s overall approach or argument; a systematically developed body, organised into clearly delineated paragraphs each addressing a specific aspect or sub-argument of the overall topic, generally moving from more general to more specific points, or following some other clear, logical organisational principle; and a well-crafted conclusion (ikhtitam) that draws the essay’s argument to a satisfying close, synthesising the preceding discussion rather than merely repeating it, and often returning to broader significance or implication.

Strong Urdu essay writing draws effectively on the language’s rich rhetorical and literary resources — including apt quotation of relevant poetry (particularly from major poets studied elsewhere in this subject, such as Iqbal, Ghalib, or Faiz, where genuinely relevant to the essay’s argument, connecting the essay’s exposition to the broader Urdu literary tradition), appropriate use of idiom and proverb, and a register and vocabulary suited to the specific topic and its intended audience — while avoiding both excessive ornamentation that obscures clear argument and excessively plain, underdeveloped prose that fails to demonstrate genuine command of formal Urdu prose style.
Common essay topics and preparation strategy.

Examination essay topics typically span social, political, cultural, and moral themes relevant to contemporary Pakistani society and broader human experience, meaning effective preparation requires developing genuine, well-organised knowledge and considered opinion across a range of significant contemporary and perennial topics, alongside practising the specific structural and stylistic conventions of formal Urdu essay composition, rather than relying on generic, loosely applicable content that fails to engage the specific essay topic with genuine depth and relevant, well-organised argument.

items.text: Effective Urdu essay writing requires a clear structure: an engaging introduction establishing significance, a systematically organised body developing the argument through clearly delineated paragraphs, and a synthesising conclusion.

Strong stylistic execution draws on Urdu’s rhetorical resources — apt poetic quotation, idiom, and register suited to the topic — while avoiding both excessive ornamentation and underdeveloped plainness.

Effective preparation requires developing genuine, well-organised knowledge across significant contemporary and perennial topics alongside practising formal Urdu essay structural and stylistic conventions.
